name: Argentina
note: Civil registries are run by the provinces under a single national law (Ley 26.413). The attending physician certifies the death, relatives (or the establishment) register it within two business days, and the registrar issues the burial licence. Registries must communicate each death to RENAPER, the national identity register. RENAPER forwards deceased electors to the electoral registry and sells a death-notice web service to pension-paying agents.

steps.title: Physician issues the certificado de defunción
steps.who: The physician who attended the last illness; failing that, another physician or authorised health agent who personally verified the death and its causes.
steps.summary: The medical death certificate proves the death; it states immediate, intermediate and underlying causes (or that they are unknown), on secure forms supplied by provincial governments.

steps.title: Certifier verifies the deceased's identity against the DNI
steps.who: The physician or authority issuing the death certificate.
steps.summary: The certifier must check the deceased's identity against the DNI and write its number on the certificate; failing the DNI, fingerprints or two witnesses. Breach is an offence (art. 32).

steps.title: Register the death within two business days
steps.who: The spouse, descendants, ascendants and relatives; failing them, any capable person who saw the body or in whose home the death occurred.

deadline.text: within two business days of the death (late up to 60 days by administrative authorisation)

steps.summary: Registration before the civil registry of the place of death within two business days; the provincial directorate may authorise late registration up to 60 days, after which a court order is needed.

steps.title: Hospital or prison administrator registers deaths on the premises
steps.who: Administrators of hospitals, prisons or any other public or private establishment.

deadline.text: within two business days of the death

steps.summary: Heads of establishments are themselves obliged to seek registration of deaths that occur there.

steps.title: Judicial authority intervenes in traumatic or suspicious deaths
steps.who: The civil registry officer; the competent judicial (or police) authority.
steps.trigger: A traumatic death, or suspicion from the certificate or circumstances of an unlawful act.
steps.summary: The judiciary must intervene in traumatic deaths and decides the disposal of the remains; where an unlawful act is suspected the registrar notifies the judicial or police authority and withholds the burial licence until the court allows it.

steps.title: Registrar issues the burial or cremation licence
steps.who: The civil registry officer of the place of death.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death (or, in urgency, the medical certificate, with registration within two business days after).
steps.summary: The licencia de inhumación o cremación is issued against the death entry, and cemeteries and crematoria must demand it.

steps.title: Registrar reports deaths from notifiable disease
steps.who: The civil registry officer, to the competent health authority.
steps.trigger: Death from a disease of public-health concern.
steps.summary: The registrar informs the health authority immediately, and still issues the burial licence.

steps.title: Registry supplies vital-statistics data
steps.summary: The civil registry must provide the data for vital statistics on deaths, infant deaths and fetal deaths.

steps.title: Copies of the death entry (partida de defunción)
steps.who: The provincial civil registry; third parties must show a legitimate interest to consult the books.
steps.summary: Registry certificates and copies are public instruments that no authority or private entity may retain. Consulting the register requires a legitimate interest.

steps.title: Registries communicate the death to RENAPER
steps.who: The 24 provincial (and CABA) civil registries, to the Registro Nacional de las Personas.
steps.summary: Every authority recording civil-status facts must communicate them to RENAPER with the act's testimony, and RENAPER records the death against the person's identity file. RENAPER's death database is built from the 24 registries' notices.

steps.title: RENAPER sends the list of deceased electors
steps.who: RENAPER or its regional delegates, to the electoral registration offices.
steps.trigger: Recording of the death by RENAPER.
steps.summary: RENAPER forwards lists of deceased electors to the electoral registries.

steps.title: ANSES learns of deaths of beneficiaries
steps.trigger: Recording of the death by RENAPER.
steps.summary: ANSES is understood to cross-check its beneficiaries against RENAPER's death data, but no official ANSES or SINTyS text was reached. The RENAPER notice service for pension-paying agents is sourced (see ar-pension-agents).

steps.title: RENAPER death-notice service for pension-paying agents
steps.who: Entities that are paying agents of pension benefits (agentes de pago de prestaciones previsionales), under RENAPER's model agreement, for a fee.
steps.trigger: A query by DNI and sex.
steps.summary: Through its Sistema de Identidad Digital, RENAPER answers DNI and sex queries with date and status of death: fallecido, observado, anticipado, presunto or no notice. Only pension-paying agents may sign up.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Two business days from the death; late registration up to 60 days by administrative authorisation, later only by court order.

informantDuty.note: Spouse and relatives first, then any capable person who saw the body or in whose home the death occurred; heads of hospitals, prisons and other establishments for deaths there.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of certificates; traumatic or suspicious deaths go to the judicial authority.

electronicRegistration.note: Registration is by book entry with a copy that may be an archivo informático; RENAPER refers to a digital death-notice system. Provincial e-registration practice not examined.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Registro Nacional de las Personas (RENAPER)
centralPopulationRegister.note: Registro Nacional de las Personas (RENAPER), which records deaths communicated by the provincial registries.

governmentPropagation.note: Registries must communicate deaths to RENAPER, which notifies electoral registries and serves death notices to pension payers; the ANSES link itself was not verified.

certificateAccess.note: Third parties must show a legitimate interest to consult registry records; the law does not separately list who may obtain a death partida.

privateSectorVerification.note: RENAPER's paid death-notice web service is open only to pension-paying agents; RENAPER may also sell specialised information to private entities.

gaps: ANSES / SINTyS: no official text found establishing how ANSES receives deaths (only parliamentary bills on hcdn.gob.ar, which are not law). anses.gob.ar is blocked by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403). Step ar-anses is unverified.
AFIP/ARCA (tax): no rule found on how the tax authority learns of deaths.
Ley 17.671 art. 19 leaves deadlines and form of communication to RENAPER to regulation; the regulatory decree was not read.
Who may obtain a death partida is set by provincial rules; Ley 26.413 only requires legitimate interest to consult the books (art. 9).
